author: HSinghHira
tagline: The fastest wiki and knowledge base for growing teams, self-hosted.
description:
Outline is a fast, beautifully designed wiki and knowledge base for teams - real-time collaborative editing, nested collections, and powerful search, all running on infrastructure you control.

**Features**
- Real-time collaborative document editing with a clean Markdown
  editor.

- Nested collections and documents, full-text search, and a
  keyboard-first interface.

- Sign-in via OIDC, Google, Slack, or Azure - no built-in
  password auth.

- API for integrations and automation.
- PostgreSQL for documents and metadata, Redis for caching and
  background jobs, and local file storage for uploads.

- Persistent storage for the database, cache, and uploaded files
  under /DATA/AppData/$AppID.


**How to use?**
1. Before installing, set up an OIDC application (or Google, Slack,
   or Azure app) - Outline requires at least one sign-in method
   configured to start. Pocket ID works well if you have it
   installed.

2. Fill in the OIDC client ID, secret, and endpoint URLs in the app
   configuration.

3. Open Outline from the Zima OS dashboard.
4. Sign in with your configured provider to create the first
   workspace.

5. Create your first collection and start writing documents.
6. Invite teammates and configure further settings, like the
   workspace logo, from the in-app admin panel under Settings.

before_install.en_US:
1. Install Pocket ID first if you want to use Pocket ID for signing in.
   Pocket ID must be accessible over a secure HTTPS connection before
   configuring it for Outline. For example:
   https://id.example.com

   Do not use an HTTP-only Pocket ID URL for your production setup.

2. Open Pocket ID and complete its initial setup. Create your Pocket ID
   account and make sure you can sign in successfully before continuing.

3. In Pocket ID, create an OIDC client for Outline.

   Go to the OIDC Clients section and create a new client.

   Use a name such as:
   Outline

   Set the redirect/callback URI to:
   https://outline.example.com/auth/oidc.callback

   Replace outline.example.com with the domain you will actually use
   to access your Outline installation.

4. After creating the OIDC client, copy the following values from Pocket ID:

   - Client ID
   - Client Secret

   Keep the client secret private. Do not publish it or share it
   publicly.

5. Make sure the Outline OIDC client in Pocket ID allows your Pocket ID
   user to access the application.

   If Pocket ID has an Allowed User Groups or access-control option,
   either allow the appropriate group containing your user or select
   unrestricted access.

   If your user is not allowed to access the OIDC client, Pocket ID
   may show:
   "You are not allowed to access this service."

6. Open the Outline app configuration in ZimaOS before starting the
   installation.

7. In the outline service, configure the OIDC settings.

   For Pocket ID, use:

   OIDC_AUTH_URI:
   https://id.example.com/authorize

   OIDC_TOKEN_URI:
   https://id.example.com/api/oidc/token

   OIDC_USERINFO_URI:
   https://id.example.com/api/oidc/userinfo

   Replace id.example.com with your Pocket ID domain.

8. Enter the OIDC credentials from Pocket ID:

   OIDC_CLIENT_ID:
   Your Pocket ID client ID

   OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET:
   Your Pocket ID client secret

9. Set the OIDC display name. For example:

   OIDC_DISPLAY_NAME:
   Pocket ID

10. Set the OIDC scopes to:

    OIDC_SCOPES:
    openid profile email groups

    The "groups" scope can be used when Pocket ID group information
    is needed by the application.

11. Set OIDC_USERNAME_CLAIM to:

    OIDC_USERNAME_CLAIM:
    preferred_username

12. Find URL in the outline service and set it to the public HTTPS
    address you will use to access Outline.

    For example:

    URL:
    https://outline.example.com

    If you are using a reverse proxy, do not use the internal Docker
    address here. URL should be the address users actually open in
    their browser.

13. Make sure your Outline domain has a valid HTTPS certificate and
    that the reverse proxy forwards HTTPS traffic to the Outline
    container.

    Example:

    https://outline.example.com
              ↓
       Reverse Proxy
              ↓
    http://your-server-ip:8437

14. In Pocket ID, make sure the OIDC redirect/callback URL exactly
    matches the Outline URL.

    Example:

    https://outline.example.com/auth/oidc.callback

    A mismatch between these URLs can prevent OIDC login from working.

15. Find SECRET_KEY and UTILS_SECRET in the outline service. They are
    pre-filled with random values.

    For a new installation, you can replace them with your own secure
    random values. You can generate secure random values using:
    https://randomkeygen.com/

    Keep these values private and do not publish them.

16. Find POSTGRES_PASSWORD in the postgres service and replace it with
    your own secure password.

    Then update the password in DATABASE_URL in the outline service
    so that both passwords match.

    Example:

    POSTGRES_PASSWORD:
    your-secure-password

    DATABASE_URL:
    postgres://outline:your-secure-password@postgres:5432/outline

17. Important: if PostgreSQL has already been initialized, changing
    POSTGRES_PASSWORD in the ZimaOS configuration does not change the
    password stored inside the existing PostgreSQL database.

    Only change this value on a new installation, or update the
    existing PostgreSQL user's password separately.

18. Start the Outline installation.

19. Wait approximately 20 to 30 seconds for PostgreSQL, Redis, and
    Outline to start completely. The first startup may take longer
    while the database is initialized.

20. Open Outline using your configured HTTPS address.

    Example:

    https://outline.example.com

21. Select "Pocket ID" (or the OIDC display name you configured) and
    sign in using your Pocket ID account.

22. On the first successful login, Outline will create the initial
    workspace for you.

23. If Pocket ID displays:
    "You are not allowed to access this service."

    Open Pocket ID and check the Outline OIDC client's access settings.
    Make sure your user is included in an allowed group or that the
    client is configured for unrestricted access.

24. If you receive a redirect URI or callback error, check that the
    callback URL configured in Pocket ID exactly matches:

    https://outline.example.com/auth/oidc.callback

    Replace outline.example.com with your actual Outline domain.

25. More settings, including workspace branding, members, permissions,
    and other administration options, are available inside Outline
    under Settings.

26. Security recommendation: use HTTPS for both Pocket ID and Outline
    when they are exposed outside your local network. Do not publish
    your OIDC client secret, database password, SECRET_KEY, or
    UTILS_SECRET in public repositories or screenshots.
